report.source_text: Postoperative CT scan showed the left thyroid lobe and the haematoma was excised. She was weaned off mechanical ventilation and extubated on the fourth postoperative day. The patient was discharged on postoperative day 10. On follow-up, the patient had complete resolution of compressive symptoms and hoarseness. The blood calcium results were in normal ranges after the partial thyroidectomy. Repeat neck ultrasonography after 1 month showed no mass in the neck.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old woman with ESRD and a 1-year history of nodular goiter presented acutely with large neck swelling, hoarseness, and progressive dysphagia. Physical exam showed a large nodular goiter without lymphadenopathy. Thyroid function tests were normal. Imaging (ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT) revealed multiple thyroid nodules and a well-defined, nonenhancing mass behind the trachea compressing the airway and esophagus. Urgent endotracheal intubation was required due to airway compression. An urgent partial thyroidectomy was performed safely despite ESRD risks. Postoperative CT confirmed excision of the left thyroid lobe and hematoma. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 4 and discharged on day 10 with complete resolution of symptoms. Postoperative histopathology confirmed spontaneous hemorrhage within a multinodular goiter.
